introduction-from-scripts-to-policy.core: AWS Backup replaces per-service backup scripts with central policy: backup plans define schedules, retention and copies; resource assignments select resources by tags or ARNs across EC2, EBS, RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, S3 and more; and Organizations backup policies apply them across accounts with central reporting.

first_principles.problem: Each team scripts its own snapshots; some forget, retention is inconsistent and audits fail.
truths: Manual scripts drift and fail silently.

analogy.title: A building's automatic sprinkler system
analogy.story: Instead of people remembering to carry buckets, coverage is built in everywhere.
analogy.breaks: Sprinklers activate on fire; backups must also be restored to prove they work.

example.title: Tag-based coverage
flow: Monthly, keep 1 year, move to cold after 90 days

check.q: How do you include resources in an AWS Backup plan at scale?
check.a: Resource assignments using tags (or ARNs), ideally applied via Organizations backup policies.

cross-region-cross-account-copies.core: Backup plans can copy recovery points to vaults in other regions (regional disaster) and other accounts (account compromise or deletion). A dedicated, locked-down backup account owned by a separate team, with its own KMS keys, means attackers who compromise production can't delete the copies.

first_principles.problem: Ransomware with admin access to the production account deletes both resources and their backups.
truths: Same-account backups share the blast radius.
derivation: Copy to a **central backup account** vault.
Use **separate KMS keys** in the destination.

analogy.title: Keeping copies of house deeds in a bank safe-deposit box in another city
analogy.story: A fire or burglar at home can't reach them.
analogy.breaks: Safe-deposit boxes need a visit; restores from copies can be automated.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Copies survive loss of the production account and region.

check.q: Why copy backups to a different account?
check.a: So compromise or deletion of the production account can't destroy the backups.

vault-lock-the-indestructible-safety-net.core: Backup Vault Lock enforces WORM on a vault: minimum and maximum retention, and prevention of deleting recovery points or changing lifecycle, even by root. Governance mode can be removed by authorised users; compliance mode becomes immutable after a cooling-off period (grace time). It's built for ransomware resilience and regulations.

first_principles.problem: A compromised admin shortens retention and deletes recovery points before the attack.
truths: Privileged users can normally delete backups.
derivation: Set a **grace time** to test before it locks.

analogy.title: A time-locked safe
analogy.story: Once the timer is set and confirmed, nobody, not even the owner, can open it early.
analogy.breaks: Safes can be drilled; compliance-mode vaults can't be unlocked by AWS support either.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: After 3 days, nobody can delete backups younger than 35 days.

check.q: What happens after the grace time in compliance mode?
check.a: The lock becomes immutable and can't be changed or removed by anyone.

backup-plans-schedules-and-lifecycle-rul.core: Backup plan rules set frequency (cron or hourly/daily/weekly), backup windows (start and completion), retention (delete after N days), lifecycle to cold storage (for supported resources), copy actions and continuous backup (PITR for RDS, S3, Aurora) where available. Multiple rules give tiered retention (daily 35 d, monthly 1 y, yearly 7 y).

first_principles.problem: One daily rule with 7-year retention makes storage costs explode.
truths: Cold storage is cheaper but has minimums.
derivation: **Cold storage** after 90+ days (min 90 days in cold).

analogy.title: Keeping photos
analogy.story: Every day's photos for a month, one per month for a year and one per year forever.
analogy.breaks: Photos are free to keep; backups cost per GB-month.

example.title: Tiered plan
flow: Daily 03:00, keep 35 days, continuous backup on
Yearly Jan 1, keep 7 years, cold after 90

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Compliance met at a fraction of cost.

example.outcome: right recovery points at the right cost.
